answer: Behavioral terrace clustering. Agents are grouped by their first-week call graph; a tight cluster whose members later fan out to the same fresh counterparties is flagged. Enforcement: transactions from flagged clusters are delayed and re-verified, and cluster members inherit each other's flags—so one identity's history contaminates its neighbors. Each new identity must therefore age on a clean jetty of isolated activity before it can join the main harbor of trade, costing attackers weeks of separate, low-value transactions per fake account and splitting their coordination budget.
